questions.question: Under the Pradhan Mantri Bhartiya Janaushadhi Pariyojana, how many Jan Aushadhi Kendras (JAKs) have been opened till 28 February 2025 across India, having an end-to-end IT-enabled supply chain system?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**15,057**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Pradhan Mantri Bhartiya Janaushadhi Pariyojana (PMBJP)** has achieved a significant milestone by opening **15,057** **Jan Aushadhi Kendras (JAKs)** across the country as of **28 February 2025**.
 
• This scheme is a flagship initiative of the **Department of Pharmaceuticals**, **Ministry of Chemicals and Fertilizers**, Government of India, aimed at providing quality generic medicines at affordable prices.
 
• The **Pharmaceuticals and Medical Devices Bureau of India (PMBI)** is the implementing agency that oversees the establishment and operations of these kendras.
 
• The network utilizes an **end-to-end IT-enabled supply chain system**, which includes a centralized **Warehouse Management System (WMS)** and **SAP-based inventory tracking** to ensure the timely availability of medicines.
 
• By **February 2025**, the coverage of the scheme has expanded to almost every district in **India**, significantly reducing the out-of-pocket expenditure on healthcare for the common man.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Product Basket:** The PMBJP product basket has grown extensively and currently includes more than **2,000 medicines** and over **300 surgical devices**, covering all major therapeutic groups such as anti-diabetics, cardiovascular drugs, and antibiotics.
 
• **Pricing Structure:** Medicines sold at **Jan Aushadhi Kendras** are priced **50% to 90%** lower than the market prices of branded medicines, ensuring that "quality medicine is not a luxury."
 
• **Jan Aushadhi Sugam Mobile App:** The government launched a digital tool to help citizens locate the nearest **Jan Aushadhi Kendra**, check medicine availability, and compare prices of generic versus branded medicines.
 
• **Employment and Incentives:** The scheme encourages **entrepreneurship** among pharmacists and NGOs. Individual entrepreneurs are provided an incentive of up to **Rs. 5 lakhs**, and special incentives of **Rs. 2 lakhs** are given for kendras opened in **North-Eastern states**, **Himalayan areas**, and **Aspirational Districts**.
 
• **Quality Assurance:** Every batch of medicine supplied to these kendras is tested at **NABL-accredited laboratories** to ensure they meet the highest standards of safety and efficacy before reaching the public.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Historical Context:** Originally launched as the **Jan Aushadhi Scheme** in **2008**, it was later revamped and renamed as **Pradhan Mantri Bhartiya Janaushadhi Pariyojana (PMBJP)** in **2015-16** to give it more momentum and wider reach.
 
• **Supply Chain Infrastructure:** To support the **15,057** centers, the **PMBI** operates a large-scale logistics network consisting of **central warehouses** and several **regional warehouses** strategically located across different **states**.
 
• **Social Impact:** In the last few years, the scheme has saved citizens billions of rupees. For example, in the **financial year 2023-24** alone, the scheme helped consumers save approximately **Rs. 10,000 crore**.
 
• **Menstrual Hygiene:** Under the scheme, **Suvidha Oxo-biodegradable Sanitary Napkins** are sold at a nominal price of **Re. 1 per pad** to improve menstrual health among women in rural and urban areas.
</ul

questions.question: Monika Gusain won a senior executive post in which of the following Indian associations?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Supreme Court Bar Association**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Monika Gusain** was elected as a **Senior Executive Member** of the **Supreme Court Bar Association (SCBA)** in the elections held for the **2024-2025** term.
 
• The **SCBA election**, which took place in **May 2024**, is one of the most prestigious events for the legal fraternity in India, determining the leadership of the advocates practicing at the **apex court**.
 
• She is a practicing **Advocate-on-Record (AOR)** in the **Supreme Court of India**, a specialized category of lawyers authorized to file matters before the court.
 
• The **2024** elections were particularly significant as they saw the return of veteran lawyer and former Union Minister **Kapil Sibal** as the **President** of the **Supreme Court Bar Association** after several years.
 
• The executive committee of the **SCBA** consists of various posts, including **President**, **Vice President**, **Honorary Secretary**, and several **Executive Members** (both **Senior** and **Junior**) who manage the affairs of the association.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Supreme Court Bar Association (SCBA)**:
 
 
• The **SCBA** is an entity that represents the collective interests of the lawyers practicing in the **Supreme Court of India**, located in **New Delhi**.
 
• It plays a critical role in maintaining the **independence of the judiciary** and ensuring the welfare of the legal community.
 
• The **SCBA** is involved in organizing legal seminars, maintaining library facilities for members, and acting as a liaison between the **Judges (the Bench)** and the **Lawyers (the Bar)**.
 
 
 
• **Other Organizations Mentioned**:

• **Indian Institute of Architects (IIA)**: The national body of **architects** in India, established in **1917**, which plays a major role in the promotion of the profession of **architecture**.
 
• **National Association of Realtors - India (NAR-INDIA)**: The apex body for **real estate consultants** in India, formed to provide a single platform for **realtors** to promote ethical practices in the **real estate sector**.
 
 
 
• **Advocate-on-Record (AOR) System**:
 
 
• Under the **Supreme Court Rules, 2013**, only an **Advocate-on-Record** is entitled to file any appearance or act for a party in the **Supreme Court**.
 
• To become an **AOR**, an advocate must have at least **four years** of practice and pass a rigorous examination conducted by the **Supreme Court of India**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

questions.question: Which of the following tennis tournaments used live electronic line calling instead of human judges in 2025?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Wimbledon**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **All England Lawn Tennis Club (AELTC)** announced in **October 2024** that it would replace human line judges with **Live Electronic Line Calling (Live ELC)** starting from the **2025** Championships.
 
• This historic decision ends **147 years** of tradition at **Wimbledon**, where line judges in their iconic uniforms have been a staple of the grass-court tournament since its inception in **1877**. ***Hence, the statement regarding Wimbledon is correct.***
 
• The new **Live ELC** system will be utilized on all **18 show courts** as well as the **qualifying** rounds held at **Roehampton**.
 
• The move is designed to ensure maximum accuracy in officiating, providing a consistent environment for players who have become accustomed to the technology on the **ATP** and **WTA** tours.
 
• Approximately **300 line judges** who worked the tournament annually will no longer be required, though **Chair Umpires** will remain in place to manage the match and keep the official score.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Australian Open and US Open:**
 
 
• The **Australian Open** became the first **Grand Slam** to entirely replace line judges with **Live ELC** in **2021**, partly as a response to the **COVID-19 pandemic** to reduce on-court personnel.
 
• The **US Open** followed suit in **2021**, adopting the technology across all its courts in **New York** to streamline play and reduce officiating errors.
 
 
 
• **The French Open (Roland Garros):**
 
 
• As of **2025**, the **French Open** remains the only **Grand Slam** to continue using human line judges.
 
• Because it is played on **clay**, the tournament relies on the physical mark the ball leaves on the surface, which the **Chair Umpire** can manually inspect if a call is disputed.
 
 
 
• **ATP Tour Mandate:**
 
 
• The **ATP Tour** (men’s professional circuit) previously announced a universal mandate that all **ATP** events must adopt **Electronic Line Calling** by the year **2025**.
 
• This policy aims to provide uniformity across various surfaces and tournament tiers, from **ATP 250** to **Masters 1000** events.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Hawk-Eye Technology:** Most **Live ELC** systems are powered by **Hawk-Eye Innovations**, which uses multiple high-speed cameras to track the trajectory of the ball and trigger an automated "out" voice call within **one-tenth of a second**.
 
• **Removal of Challenges:** With the implementation of **Live ELC**, the traditional "challenge" system (where players ask for a video review) is eliminated, as every call is essentially a real-time review.
 
• **Game Speed:** Data indicates that **Live ELC** significantly speeds up the duration of matches by reducing the time spent on disputes and the physical movement of line judges during changeovers.
 
• **Preservation of Tradition:** While **Wimbledon** is moving to digital officiating, the **AELTC** emphasized that the **Chair Umpire** remains the final authority on court for matters of conduct and scorekeeping.

questions.question: What responsibility did the Supreme Court give to the National Environmental Engineering Research Institute (NEERI) in April 2025?

options.text: To study the impact of glass industries on the Taj Mahal
To relocate glass factories near the Taj Mahal
To promote tourism near the Taj Mahal

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**To study the impact of glass industries on the Taj Mahal**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In **April 2025**, the **Supreme Court of India** issued a directive to the **National Environmental Engineering Research Institute (NEERI)** to conduct a detailed scientific assessment.
 
• The primary responsibility assigned to **NEERI** was to **study the impact of glass industries** on the structural integrity and aesthetic preservation of the **Taj Mahal**.
 
• This study focuses on the environmental footprint of industrial units located within the **Taj Trapezium Zone (TTZ)**, specifically those involved in glass manufacturing in nearby regions like **Firozabad**. ***Hence, the statement regarding the impact of glass industries is correct.***
 
• The **Supreme Court** aims to determine if the emissions from these industries are contributing to the yellowing of the marble or "**marble cancer**," caused by chemical reactions with pollutants.
 
• **NEERI** is expected to provide data-driven recommendations on whether existing pollution control equipment in these factories is sufficient or if stricter regulations are required to protect the **UNESCO World Heritage Site**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **National Environmental Engineering Research Institute (NEERI):**
 
 
• It was established in **1958** and is headquartered in **Nagpur**, **Maharashtra**.
 
• It functions under the **Council of Scientific and Industrial Research (CSIR)** and focuses on environmental monitoring, hazardous waste management, and environmental impact assessments.
 
• **NEERI** has been frequently consulted by the **Indian Judiciary** for expert technical opinions on environmental conservation cases.
 
 
 
• **The Taj Trapezium Zone (TTZ):**
 
 
• The **TTZ** is a defined area of approximately **10,400 square kilometers** around the **Taj Mahal**.
 
• It encompasses several districts including **Agra**, **Firozabad**, **Mathura**, **Hathras**, and **Etah** in **Uttar Pradesh**, as well as **Bharatpur** in **Rajasthan**.
 
• The zone was established following the **1996 Supreme Court** judgment to protect the monument from pollution-induced damage.
 
 
 
• **Glass Industry in Firozabad:**
 
 
• **Firozabad** is known as the "**Glass City of India**" due to its extensive cluster of glass-making units and bangle factories.
 
• Historically, these industries used **coal** and **coke**, which emitted high levels of **Sulfur Dioxide (SO2)** and **particulate matter**, posing a direct threat to the white marble of the **Taj Mahal**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Legal Precedents:** The protection of the **Taj Mahal** is governed by the landmark case of **M.C. Mehta vs. Union of India**, filed in the **1980s**, which led to the closure of several polluting industries.
 
• **Transition to Cleaner Fuel:** The **Supreme Court** previously mandated that industries in the **TTZ** must switch from traditional fuels to **Piped Natural Gas (PNG)** to minimize the carbon footprint and acidic emissions.
 
• **Marble Cancer:** This term refers to the corrosion of marble by **acid rain** (formed by **Sulfur Dioxide** and **Nitrogen Oxides** reacting with water vapor), which converts calcium carbonate into calcium sulfate, causing the surface to flake and turn yellow.
 
• **Current Status:** The **April 2025** order signifies the court's ongoing vigilance in balancing industrial economic activity with the preservation of **India's** cultural heritage through rigorous scientific auditing by **CSIR-NEERI**.
</ul

questions.question: Which earthquake rescue operation by the National Response force in myanmar in March 2025?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Operation Bramha**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Operation Bramha** was a high-stakes humanitarian mission launched by the **Government of India** in **March 2025** to provide immediate relief to **Myanmar** following a devastating **earthquake**.
 
• The **National Disaster Response Force (NDRF)** spearheaded the mission, deploying multiple specialized teams equipped with **advanced search and rescue tools**, including **canine squads** and **chip-based life detectors**.
 
• The operation focused on the hardest-hit regions of **Myanmar**, where the seismic activity caused extensive damage to infrastructure and residential buildings, requiring **urban search and rescue (USAR)** expertise.
 
• India utilized the **C-17 Globemaster III** aircraft of the **Indian Air Force** to transport over **100 personnel**, along with emergency **medical supplies**, **tents**, and **ready-to-eat meals** to the affected zones.
 
• This mission reinforces India's role as the **"First Responder"** in the **Indian Ocean Region** and its commitment to the **"Neighborhood First"** policy during natural calamities.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **National Disaster Response Force (NDRF)**:
 
 
• The **NDRF** was constituted in the year **2006** under the **Disaster Management Act, 2005**, specifically for the purpose of specialized response to natural and man-made disasters.
 
• It operates under the **Ministry of Home Affairs** and is headquartered in **New Delhi**, with various battalions stationed across **India** for rapid deployment.
 
 
 
• **India-Myanmar Relations in Disaster Management**:
 
 
• India has a history of assisting **Myanmar**, such as during **Cyclone Mocha** in **2023** under **Operation Karuna**, where **Indian Navy** ships delivered essential relief materials.
 
• The collaboration between the two nations is vital due to their shared **1,643 km long land border** and proximity in the **Bay of Bengal**.
 
 
 
• **Humanitarian Assistance and Disaster Relief (HADR)**:
 
 
• **HADR** operations are a core component of India's **soft power** diplomacy, demonstrating technical capability and regional leadership.
 
• Other notable operations include **Operation Dost** (the **2023 Turkey-Syria earthquake**) and **Operation Maitri** (the **2015 Nepal earthquake**).
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Seismic Vulnerability**: **Myanmar** is located in a seismically active zone where the **Indian Plate** subducts under the **Burma Microplate**, making it prone to high-magnitude earthquakes.
 
• **Technical Coordination**: The success of **Operation Bramha** relied on the **Ministry of External Affairs (MEA)** coordinating with the **Myanmar** authorities to ensure a seamless "green corridor" for aid delivery.
 
• **Medical Aid**: A significant part of the relief package included **Level-2 and Level-3 medical facilities** capable of performing emergency surgeries in field conditions.
 
• **Global Standards**: **NDRF** teams follow the guidelines of the **International Search and Rescue Advisory Group (INSARAG)**, ensuring that their methods are compatible with international disaster response protocols.
</ul

__
 
• The **Corruption Perceptions Index (CPI) 2024** was released by the global civil society organization **Transparency International** in **February 2025**.
 
• **India** recorded a score of **38** out of **100** in the **2024** index, reflecting the perceived level of public sector corruption in the country.
 
• In comparison to the **2023** report, where India scored **39**, the current score of **38** indicates a slight decline in the perceived integrity of the public sector.
 
• India’s rank in the **2024** index is **93rd** among **180 countries** and territories evaluated globally.
 
• The index uses a scale where **0** represents "highly corrupt" and **100** represents "very clean," placing India in the lower half of the global rankings.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Transparency International:**
 
 
• It is an international non-governmental organization based in **Berlin, Germany**, founded in **1993**.
 
• The organization aims to take action to combat global corruption and prevent criminal activities arising from corruption.
 
• It publishes various reports including the **Global Corruption Barometer** and the **Corruption Perceptions Index**.

• More than **two-thirds** of countries score below **50**, highlighting serious corruption issues worldwide.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **CPI Methodology:**
 
 
• The index aggregates data from **13 external sources**, including the **World Bank**, the **World Economic Forum**, and private risk and consulting companies.
 
• It focuses specifically on **public sector corruption**, including bribery, diversion of public funds, and the use of public office for private gain.
 
 
 
• **Regional Context (South Asia):**
 
 
• Within **South Asia**, **India** (**38**) and **Maldives** (**39**) often share similar score ranges, while **Pakistan** and **Bangladesh** typically record significantly lower scores.
 
• The **2024** report emphasized that the decline in **justice system** independence is a key driver for lower scores in many democratic nations.
 
 
 
• **Impact of Corruption:**
 
 
• A low score in the **Corruption Perceptions Index** can negatively impact a country's **Foreign Direct Investment (FDI)** and overall **economic growth**.
 
• Corruption is frequently linked to social inequality and the erosion of **democratic institutions**.

questions.question: According to the Global Peace Index 2025, which of the following countries at the bottom, indicating the least peaceful nation?
questions.solution:
p>The correct answer is __**Russia**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• According to the **Global Peace Index (GPI) 2025**, **Russia** is ranked at the bottom of the list, indicating it as the least peaceful nation among the provided options due to its sustained **military aggression** and **internal suppression**.
 
• The index is an annual publication by the **Institute for Economics and Peace (IEP)**, a global think tank based in **Sydney, Australia**, which evaluates **163 independent states and territories**.
 
• Russia's ranking has deteriorated significantly since the full-scale **invasion of Ukraine** in **February 2022**, leading to massive increases in **battlefield deaths** and **military expenditure**. ***Hence, the statement regarding Russia is correct.***
 
• The evaluation is based on three thematic domains: **Societal Safety and Security**, **Ongoing Domestic and International Conflict**, and **Militarization**.
 
• While **Yemen**, **Sudan**, and **Syria** have consistently been among the most violent regions, the intensity of **international conflict** and **geopolitical isolation** has moved Russia to the bottom tiers of the index in the **2025** report.
 
• Russia’s score is negatively impacted by high levels of **political instability**, **violent demonstrations**, and a surge in **internal security** measures to maintain control during wartime.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Structure of the GPI**:
 
 
• The index was first launched in **May 2007** and remains the world's leading measure of global peacefulness, covering **99.7% of the world's population**.
 
• It utilizes **23 qualitative and quantitative indicators**, such as **homicide rates**, **access to weapons**, and **refugee populations**.
 
 
 
• **Most Peaceful Nations**:
 
 
• **Iceland** has consistently held the title of the **most peaceful country** in the world since **2008**.
 
• Other highly peaceful nations often include **Denmark**, **Ireland**, **New Zealand**, and **Austria**, which benefit from **low corruption** and **high transparency**.
 
 
 
• **Economic Impact of Violence**:
 
 
• The **IEP** calculates the **economic cost of violence**, which includes the loss of **GDP** and expenses related to **military** and **internal security**.
 
• For nations like **Russia** and **Ukraine**, the economic impact of the **war** has exceeded **30% to 60% of their respective GDPs** in recent years.
 
 
 
• **Regional Trends**:
 
 
• The **Middle East and North Africa (MENA)** region remained the least peaceful region for several years, though **Europe** has seen the largest regional deterioration in peace due to the **war in Eurasia**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Negative vs. Positive Peace**:
 
 
• **Negative Peace** is defined as the **absence of violence** or fear of violence, which is what the **GPI** primarily measures.
 
• **Positive Peace** refers to the **attitudes, institutions, and structures** that create and sustain peaceful societies, such as a **well-functioning government** and **sound business environment**.
 
 
 
• **Conflict in Sudan and Yemen**:
 
 
• **Sudan** experienced a sharp decline in peacefulness following the outbreak of **civil war** in **April 2023** between the **Sudanese Armed Forces (SAF)** and the **Rapid Support Forces (RSF)**.
 
• **Yemen** remains a critical humanitarian concern, though it has seen slight fluctuations in its ranking depending on the intensity of the **Houthi-led conflict**.
 
 
 
• **Militarization Domain**:
 
 
• This domain measures the **military capacity** of a country, including **nuclear weapons capability** and **arms exports**. **Russia** scores very poorly in this domain due to its status as a major **nuclear power** and its massive **arms production**.

questions.question: In the Union Budget 2025-26, the Government of India announced which of the following missions for ensuring energy reliability and reducing dependency on fossil fuels?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Nuclear Energy Mission**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• During the presentation of the **Union Budget 2025-26**, Union Finance Minister **Nirmala Sitharaman** announced the **Nuclear Energy Mission** as a core component of India's strategy for **energy security** and **transition**.
 
• The mission focuses on the development of **Bharat Small Reactors (BSR)**, which are designed to provide decentralized and reliable power, particularly for hard-to-abate industries.
 
• A significant highlight of this mission is the promotion of **Public-Private Partnerships (PPP)**, allowing the private sector to collaborate with the government in **research and development** and the deployment of nuclear technologies.
 
• The government aims to leverage **Nuclear Energy** to reduce the carbon footprint of the industrial sector, supporting the national goal of achieving **Net Zero emissions by 2070**.
 
• This initiative is part of a broader **Energy Transition Roadmap** that seeks to balance the intermittency of renewable sources like solar and wind with stable **baseload power** from nuclear sources. ***Hence, the correct answer is Nuclear Energy Mission.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Small Modular Reactors (SMRs):**
 
 
• **SMRs** are advanced nuclear reactors that have a power capacity of up to **300 MW** per unit, which is about one-third of the generating capacity of traditional nuclear power reactors.
 
• Due to their **small size**, they can be factory-constructed and transported to a site for installation, making them more affordable and flexible in terms of **location** compared to large-scale plants.
 
 
 
• **PM Surya Ghar Muft Bijli Yojana:**
 
 
• Announced previously and reinforced in recent fiscal discussions, this scheme aims to provide **300 units of free electricity** every month to **1 crore households** through **rooftop solar** installations.
 
• It represents a massive push toward **Renewable Energy** at the consumer level, reducing the burden on the national grid and promoting self-reliance.
 
 
 
• **Hydrogen Mission (National Green Hydrogen Mission):**
 
 
• Launched in **January 2023** with an outlay of **Rs. 19,744 crore**, this mission aims to make India a global hub for the production and export of **Green Hydrogen**.
 
• The target is to reach a production capacity of **5 Million Metric Tonnes (MMT)** per annum by **2030**.
 
 
 
• **Net Zero Target 2070:**
 
 
• India committed to this target at the **COP26** summit in **Glasgow**. The transition involves shifting the **energy mix** from fossil fuels (coal, oil) to non-fossil sources (solar, wind, nuclear, and hydro).
 
• As of **2024-25**, India has one of the world's fastest-growing renewable energy capacities, ranking **4th** globally in total installed renewable energy capacity.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Nuclear Power Corporation of India Limited (NPCIL):** A **Public Sector Enterprise** under the **Department of Atomic Energy (DAE)**, it is the primary body responsible for the design, construction, and operation of nuclear power plants in India.
 
• **Three-Stage Nuclear Power Programme:** Formulated by **Homi J. Bhabha**, this program aims to utilize India's vast **Thorium** reserves. The current phase primarily involves **Pressurized Heavy Water Reactors (PHWRs)**.
 
• **Civil Liability for Nuclear Damage Act (2010):** This act provides a framework for compensation in the event of a nuclear accident, which has been a key point of discussion regarding **Private Sector** entry into the nuclear domain.
 
• **Energy Reliability:** Unlike solar and wind, which are **intermittent**, nuclear energy provides a continuous supply of electricity, making it essential for maintaining **grid stability** as India industrializes further.
</ul

questions.question: What was the theme for Ayurveda Day, 2025, as announced by the Ministry of Ayush?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Ayurveda for People & Planet**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Ministry of Ayush** has officially announced that the theme for the **10th Ayurveda Day**, to be celebrated in **2025**, is **"Ayurveda for People & Planet"**.
 
• This theme underscores the **holistic philosophy** of Ayurveda, which views **human health** as inseparable from the **health of the environment** and the ecosystem.
 
• **Ayurveda Day** is observed globally every year on the auspicious occasion of **Dhanwantari Jayanti** (also known as **Dhanteras**), honoring the **God of Medicine** in Hindu tradition.
 
• The **2025** celebration marks the **tenth edition** of this initiative, focusing on promoting **sustainable living** through Ayurvedic principles like **Ritucharya** (seasonal guidelines) and **Aahara** (dietary habits).
 
• The primary objective of the campaign is to **internationalize Ayurveda** and establish it as a robust, **evidence-based** system of medicine that addresses modern-day **lifestyle disorders** and **climate-related health challenges**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Origin of Ayurveda Day:** The **Government of India** decided to celebrate Ayurveda Day annually starting from the **year 2016**. The first-ever Ayurveda Day was held on **October 28, 2016**.
 
• **Lord Dhanwantari:** In Indian mythology, **Lord Dhanwantari** is considered an **avatar of Lord Vishnu** who emerged during the **Samudra Manthan** (churning of the ocean) carrying the pot of **Amrit** (nectar of immortality).
 
• **Ministry of Ayush:** Formed on **9th November 2014**, the Ministry of **Ayurveda, Yoga and Naturopathy, Unani, Siddha, and Homeopathy** is responsible for the education, research, and propagation of **traditional Indian medicine**.
 
• **Previous Themes:** The theme for **2024** was **"Ayurveda Innovations for Global Health"**, while the **2023** theme focused on **"Ayurveda for One Health"** (Ayurveda for everyone on every day).
 
• **Global Recognition:** Ayurveda is recognized as one of the oldest **healthcare systems** in the world. The **World Health Organization (WHO)** has established the **Global Centre for Traditional Medicine** in **Jamnagar, Gujarat**, to integrate traditional knowledge with **modern science**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs):** The theme **"Ayurveda for People & Planet"** aligns with several **United Nations SDGs**, specifically **Goal 3** (Good Health and Well-being) and **Goal 12** (Responsible Consumption and Production).
 
• **Digital Ayurveda:** The Ministry often utilizes platforms like the **"Ayurveda Day Portal"** to track **mass participation** and global events, which have previously seen participation from over **100 countries**.
 
• **Health Promotion:** Ayurveda emphasizes **Prakriti** (individual constitution) and **Panchakarma** (detoxification), which are gaining global popularity for **preventive healthcare**.
</ul

questions.question: Where was the 2025 Open Championship (golf) played from July 17–20?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Royal Portrush, Northern Ireland**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **153rd Open Championship** is scheduled to be held from **July 17 to July 20, 2025**.
 
• The designated venue for this prestigious event is the **Royal Portrush Golf Club**, located in **County Antrim, Northern Ireland**. ***Hence, the correct answer is Royal Portrush, Northern Ireland.***
 
• This marks the **third time** in the history of the tournament that it will be hosted at this venue. The previous occasions were in **1951** and **2019**.
 
• The selection of **Royal Portrush** follows the highly successful **2019** championship, which saw record-breaking attendance and was won by **Shane Lowry**.
 
• The **R&A** (The Royal and Ancient Golf Club of St Andrews) confirmed the return to **Northern Ireland** as part of its efforts to rotate the tournament among the UK's finest links courses.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **The Open Championship:**
 
 
• Often referred to as **The British Open**, it is the **oldest** of the four major championships in professional golf, first played in **1860** at **Prestwick Golf Club**.
 
• It is the only major championship played outside the **United States** and is organized by the **R&A**.
 
• The winner is traditionally awarded the **Claret Jug** (officially the Golf Champion Trophy) and is crowned the **"Champion Golfer of the Year."**
 
 
 
• **Royal Portrush Golf Club:**
 
 
• Founded in **1888**, it features two links courses: the **Dunluce Links** (the championship course) and the **Valley Links**.
 
• The **Dunluce Links** is widely regarded as one of the most challenging and scenic courses in the world, famously redesigned by **Harry Colt** in **1929**.
 
 
 
• **The "Rota" System:**
 
 
• The Open is played on a rotation of ten coastal **links courses** across **Scotland**, **England**, and **Northern Ireland**.
 
• **St Andrews (Old Course)** is the most frequent host and typically hosts the tournament every **five years**.
 
• The **152nd Open** in **2024** was held at **Royal Troon** in **Scotland**, where **Xander Schauffele** emerged as the champion.
 
 
 
• **Future Venues:**
 
 
• Following the **2025** event at **Royal Portrush**, the **154th Open** is scheduled to take place at **Royal Birkdale** in **England** in **2026**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Economic Impact:** Hosting the **Open Championship** provides a massive boost to the local economy; the **2019** event at **Portrush** generated over **£100 million** in economic benefit for **Northern Ireland**.
 
• **Field and Qualification:** The tournament features a field of **156 players**, consisting of the world's top-ranked professionals and golfers who qualify through various **Open Qualifying Series** events globally.
 
• **Course Modifications:** In preparation for **2025**, minor modifications and infrastructure improvements are often made to the **Dunluce Links** to accommodate modern hitting distances and large spectator galleries.

questions.question: Which para-athlete was honoured with the Major Dhyan Chand Khel Ratna Award by President Droupadi Murmu at Rashtrapati Bhavan in January 2025?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Praveen Kumar**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Praveen Kumar**, the celebrated **para-high jumper**, was conferred with India's highest sporting honor, the **Major Dhyan Chand Khel Ratna Award**, for the year **2024**.
 
• The prestigious award was presented by **President Droupadi Murmu** during a ceremony held at **Rashtrapati Bhavan** in **January 2025**.
 
• The **21-year-old** athlete from **Noida**, **Uttar Pradesh**, was recognized for his extraordinary performance at the **Paris 2024 Paralympics**, where he clinched the **Gold Medal** in the **Men's High Jump T64** event.
 
• During the **Paris 2024** games, he set a new **Asian Record** by clearing a height of **2.08 meters**, securing his second consecutive Paralympic medal after winning **Silver** at the **Tokyo 2020 Paralympics**.
 
• His selection was recommended by the **National Sports Awards** committee, overseen by the **Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports**, making him the only recipient of the **Khel Ratna** for this cycle. ***Hence, the correct answer is Praveen Kumar.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Major Dhyan Chand Khel Ratna Award:**
 
 
• It is the **highest sporting honor** of the Republic of India, awarded annually by the **Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports**.
 
• The award was formerly known as the **Rajiv Gandhi Khel Ratna Award** before being renamed in **August 2021** in honor of the hockey legend **Major Dhyan Chand**.
 
• Recipients receive a **medallion**, a **certificate**, and a substantial cash prize of **Rs. 25 lakh**.
 
• It is awarded for "spectacular and most outstanding performance in the field of sports over a period of **four years**" at the international level.
 
 
 
• **National Sports Awards:**
 
 
• This umbrella of awards includes the **Arjuna Award** (for consistent outstanding performance), the **Dronacharya Award** (for eminent coaches), and the **Dhyan Chand Award for Lifetime Achievement**.
 
• Traditionally, these awards are presented on **August 29**, which is **National Sports Day**, marking the birth anniversary of **Major Dhyan Chand**, though the ceremony date can be adjusted based on the international sports calendar.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Other Nominees and Awardees:**
 
 
• **Preeti Pal:** A brilliant **para-athlete** who became the first Indian woman to win **two medals** (both **Bronze**) in track events at a single **Paralympics** (**Paris 2024**). She was honored with the **Arjuna Award** for **2024**.
 
• **Ajeet Singh:** A prominent **para-javelin thrower** who won the **Silver Medal** at the **Paris 2024 Paralympics** in the **F46 category**. He was also a recipient of the **Arjuna Award** in **January 2025**.
 
• **Subhash Rana:** A renowned **shooting coach** who has played a pivotal role in mentoring several **para-shooters** to international success, often associated with the **Dronacharya Award** discussions for his contribution to **Indian para-sports**.
 
 
 
• **Selection Process:**
 
 
• The awardees are selected by a **committee** comprising retired judges, former **Khel Ratna** winners, and sports journalists appointed by the **Government of India**.
 
• The performance of athletes in the **Olympic/Paralympic Games**, **Asian Games**, and **Commonwealth Games** carries the highest weightage in the selection criteria.
 
 
</ul
